answer: The analytic Monte Carlo checks identified as future work are the four known-answer cases in Case 5 of the Monte Carlo reference cases page, explicitly 'not yet implemented': (1) estimating pi from uniform samples with a known standard error; (2) estimating the mean of an exponential distribution with a known variance; (3) comparing an M/M/1 queue's mean wait with the analytic formula for a stable system; (4) checking empirical coverage of a confidence interval over many synthetic samples. The page states V12 'does not claim these checks' and records them as 'future verification work, not as completed evidence.' By contrast, the completed reference tests are Case 1 conservation (offered = completed + rejected + backlog), Case 2 deterministic replay (same result hash for same model/scenario/seed), Case 3 boundary cases (zero arrivals, zero servers, zero queue capacity, etc.), and Case 4 sensitivity sanity (first-order indices in [0,1]; total-order at least first-order). The page notes the current cases exercise implemented accounting, event order and sensitivity sanity, 'not the statistical calibration of the sampler.'
